description.narrative: The Independent Medical Legal Unit (IMLU) is a governance, health, and human rights non-governmental organization with a vision of having A Society free from Torture and Related Violations. Our work is fostered by a holistic approach that includes litigation, medical and psycho-social rehabilitation, socio-economic empowerment, oversight of government compliance with human rights obligations, and advocacy of political, legal, and institutional reforms that promote accountability, healing, and justice. Over the last three decades, the organization has supported more than 6,000 victims of torture, and cruel, degrading, and inhumane treatments. We have a national presence of over 300 professionals; doctors, trauma counsellors, lawyers, human rights monitors, and journalists.

activity-date.narrative: Within the period under review, IMLU engaged with various stakeholders in the justice sector to harness partnerships and collaborations that will ensure duty bearers respond to cases of torture and related violations to ensure healing and justice for victims and survivors. This was carried out through engagements on full implementation of POTA and the National Coroner Services Act (NCSA) of 2017. On POTA, IMLU held consultative forums with ODPP, DCI and the Judiciary on policing accountability through activation of charges under the Act as opposed to charging police officers under the Penal Code. A committee was formed known as the Tripartite that would oversee training of investigating officers at the DCI, IPOA, IAU and the ODPP on drafting charge sheets under POTA. Similarly, IMLU engaged in consultation with the Department of Justice on the need to review NCSA 2017 to support its implementation. The administrative functions of the Act placed the Cabinet Secretary for Justice, an office that does not exist in the republic had hindered its operationalization. To this end, the DoJ published the NCS Amendment Bill 2023 to rectify this anomaly. The Bill is set to go through the legal process for review in 2024. In order to develop and support the government in reporting on the UNCAT, IMLU convened a UPR thematic group meeting on Torture, Enforced Disappearance and Death Penalty. The forum took stock of the current development and the need to review the alternative report prepared in the 3rd cycle for sharing during the 4th Cycle of the UPR in October 2024
